questions.question: The special judicial magistrate ___ urgent bail petitions every Friday afternoon.
questions.explanation: 'Every Friday afternoon' ek recurring habitual time marker hai jo Simple Present demand karta hai. Singular subject ('The special judicial magistrate') ke saath verb mein '-s' lagta hai ('hears').
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-01: Habitual actions aur scheduled routines ke liye Simple Present use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The district judge ___ the interim stay order three days ago.
questions.explanation: 'Three days ago' beete huye time ko clearly specify karta hai, isliye yahan strictly Simple Past (V2: 'passed') aayega. Definite past time markers ke saath Present Perfect (A) use nahi ho sakta.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-05: 'Ago' completed past time batata hai, isliye Simple Past use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The court assistant ___ certified copies of the order right now.
questions.explanation: 'Right now' bolte waqt chal rahe ongoing action ko darshata hai, isliye yahan Present Continuous ('is issuing') aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-02: Speech ke moment par chal rahe live actions ke liye Present Continuous use karte hain.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The Law Department ___ the competitive examination syllabus recently.
questions.explanation: 'Recently' ek aise completed action ko batata hai jiska direct link ya relevance present situation se hai, isliye active voice mein Present Perfect ('has amended') aayega. Option C passive structure bana deta hai jo context ke hisaab se galat hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-03: Active assertive sentences mein 'recently' ke saath aamtaur par Present Perfect use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The clerk ___ the cause list when the power supply unexpectedly tripped.
questions.explanation: Past mein ek background action chal raha tha ('was compiling') jab achanak doosra event ('tripped') hua. Aise interrupted past actions ke liye background mein Past Continuous lagta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-06: Kisi shorter action se interrupt hone wale ongoing past background action ke liye Past Continuous use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The investigation agency did not ___ any incriminating emails during the server audit.
questions.explanation: Negative auxiliary 'did not' ke baad hamesha lexical verb ki base form V1 ('discover') aati hai. Option A ('discovered') double past error create karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-05: Negative Simple Past mein 'did not + V1' use karein, V2 nahi.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The advocate ___ the counter-affidavit before the bench rose for the lunch recess.
questions.explanation: Past ke do completed events mein se affidavit submit karne ka kaam bench ke uthne se pehle hua tha. Pehle complete hone wale past action ke liye Past Perfect ('had submitted') use hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-07: Jab past ke do actions 'before' ke saath jude hon, toh pehle complete hone wale action ke liye Past Perfect use karein.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: This confiscated electronic storage device ___ to the primary defendant.
questions.explanation: 'Belong' ek stative verb hai jo possession (ownership) show karta hai, iska continuous/progressive form nahi banta. Singular subject ke saath Simple Present ('belongs') aayega.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-01: Possession express karne wale stative verbs ko Simple tenses mein use kiya jata hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: By noon tomorrow, the scrutiny division ___ the list of eligible candidates.
questions.explanation: 'By noon tomorrow' future ki ek completion deadline set karta hai. Kisi future deadline se pehle poore hone wale action ke liye Future Perfect ('will have prepared') use hota hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-11: Future deadline ('by + time') tak complete hone wale action ke liye Future Perfect (will have + V3) use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The system administrators ___ the database integrity since early morning.
questions.explanation: 'Since early morning' ek aisa time duration batata hai jo past ke point se start hokar present tak continuous chal raha hai. Plural subject ke saath Present Perfect Continuous ('have been auditing') sahi hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-04: 'Since' ke saath past se present tak continue rehne wale actions ke liye Present Perfect Continuous use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: The previous computer operator ___ in the e-Courts cell for seven years before transferring to the revenue board in 2020.
questions.explanation: Context 'before transferring ... in 2020' clearly show karta hai ki 7 saal ka service period past mein hi complete khatam ho chuka tha. Jab duration ka present se koi connection na bacha ho, toh Simple Past ('served') use hota hai. Present Perfect forms (A, D) galat continuous connection suggest karti hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-05 Note: Agar past duration completely khatam ho chuki ho aur present se koi link na ho, toh Simple Past use karein.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: Choose the grammatically faultless sentence:

options.text: Yesterday at 4:00 PM, the registrar had examined the original registers.
Yesterday at 4:00 PM, the registrar was examining the original registers.
Yesterday at 4:00 PM, the registrar has examined the original registers.
Yesterday at 4:00 PM, the registrar is examining the original registers.

questions.explanation: Ek specific past timestamp ('Yesterday at 4:00 PM') jo us waqt chal rahe ongoing action ko point kare, Past Continuous ('was examining') demand karta hai. Bina prior reference event ke Past Perfect (A) galat hai, aur 'yesterday' ke saath Present Perfect (C) rule break karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-06: Past ke kisi specific clock time par chal rahe ongoing action ke liye Past Continuous use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: Spot the error: 'The judicial registrar (A) / has verified the seal (B) / on the urgent petition (C) / yesterday morning (D).'
questions.explanation: Part B mein tense discord hai. Part D ka 'yesterday morning' ek definite past time marker hai, isliye Present Perfect ('has verified') ungrammatical hai. Yahan Simple Past ('verified') hona chahiye.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-05: Definite past time markers ke saath Present Perfect use nahi kiya ja sakta; Simple Past zaroori hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Adapted from competitive examination error identification patterns

questions.question: Select the correct verb forms for the respective blanks: 'At 10:00 AM tomorrow, the committee ___ (meet) in the conference hall, and by 1:00 PM they ___ (finalize) their recommendation.'

options.text: will have met; will be finalizing
will be meeting; will have finalized

questions.explanation: Pehle clause mein future ke ek specific moment par ongoing action ki baat ho rahi hai ('At 10:00 AM tomorrow ... will be meeting' -> Future Continuous). Doosre clause mein ek future deadline di gayi hai jahan tak recommendation complete ho chuki hogi ('by 1:00 PM ... will have finalized' -> Future Perfect).
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-10 & T-11: Future ke point in time ke liye Future Continuous aur future deadline ('by + time') ke liye Future Perfect use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01

questions.question: Fill the blanks accurately: 'The clerk normally ___ (not make) procedural errors, but yesterday he ___ (overlook) a critical notification date.'
questions.explanation: Pehle clause mein routine habit ('normally') ki baat ho rahi hai: singular subject ('The clerk') ke negative sentence ke liye 'does not' + base form V1 ('does not make') aayega. Doosre clause mein definite past time marker 'yesterday' hai, jo Simple Past V2 ('overlooked') demand karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule T-01 & T-05: Simple Present negative mein 'does not + V1' aur definite past mein V2 use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L01
